name: Sanekazura root hair straightening

card.summary: A traditional Japanese hair treatment using the mucilage of the sanekazura vine to smooth, condition and hold hair, giving a sleeker, straighter look.
card.note: No clinical trials on hair straightening with this plant.

quick.overview:
Sanekazura (Kadsura japonica) is an evergreen vine native to Japan. Material extracted from it has long been used as a hair dressing, and the sanekazura juice treatment is described as smoothing and conditioning hair for a sleeker look.

Research on its use specifically for straightening has not been published. Its documented uses include hair dressing and as an ingredient in traditional Japanese paper making.
quick.how: Practitioners apply the plant's mucilage-rich extract to hair as a conditioning and smoothing dressing, in the manner of a traditional styling aid.
quick.risks: No documented adverse effects are known to this entry. As with any plant-derived topical, a patch test is the usual precaution on labels, and individual sensitivities are possible.

lead: Sanekazura (Kadsura japonica) is an evergreen climbing plant native to Japan, with glossy leaves, white flowers and bright scarlet fruit. Material extracted from it is used for hair dressing, and extracts are also used in traditional Japanese washi paper making [1].

The sanekazura juice treatment is presented as a traditional plant-based way to smooth and condition hair, helping hair lie straighter and look glossier. No published clinical studies have examined it as a straightening treatment.

chain: Plant mucilage is applied to hair
Hair is coated, smoothed and held in place
angle.text: The vine's sticky extract works as a traditional dressing that coats and smooths hair, which is how it is said to give a straighter, glossier appearance.

paras: Kadsura japonica grows in woodlands in Honshu, Kyushu and the Ryukyu Islands. The fruit is edible and the vine is grown as an ornamental. Its extracted material is used as a hair dressing [1].
